explanation: 该论文研究了住宅区与石油和天然气开发之间的邻近关系，并分析了社会经济条件。虽然它不直接涉及遥感技术，但与大气环境遥感技术中的空气质量监测和大气成分分析有间接关联，因为它关注了与石油和天然气开发相关的环境暴露和健康风险。
topic_words: ['oil and gas development', 'residential proximity', 'air quality monitoring']
authors: Lara Schwarz;Nina M Flores;David J X González;Heather McBrien;Nina Brooks;Jonathan J Buonocore;Amira Aker;Veronica Southerland;Joan A Casey;Mary D Willis
title: Residential proximity to oil and gas development and socioeconomic conditions: a comparative analysis of 33 countries
abstract: Fossil fuels continue to dominate the global energy supply. As emerging technologies drive up global energy consumption (e.g. cryptocurrency mining, data centers), identifying which populations live in residential proximity to oil and gas extraction will become increasingly important. Yet, no prior study has done so on an international scale. We combine the Oil and Gas Infrastructure Mapping database with the Global Human Settlement Layer to estimate residential proximity to oil and gas wells across 33 countries in 2024. We further link these data with indicators of income and social deprivation to examine disparities in population proximity. We estimate that 150.9 million people reside within 3 km of 4.5 million oil and gas wells across 33 countries, representing 10% of their population. Country-level residential proximity to oil and gas wells is highest in the Netherlands (38.4%), Canada (33.4%), and the United States (31.3%). Of the 33 countries, 15 had populations exposed to wells across borders, including 427 thousand Mexican residents near U.S. wells, and 185 thousand U.S. residents living near wells outside national borders. This is the first large-scale, multi-country quantification of residential exposure to oil and gas extraction, providing an evidence base for future population health research and policies to reduce risks and address energy-related inequities worldwide.

explanation: 该论文研究了青藏高原东南部和东北部夏季极端小时降水（EHP）的驱动因素，涉及海面温度（SST）强迫的环流演变，与大气环境遥感技术（如卫星观测、大气成分分析）密切相关，因此是强相关的。
authors: Jilan Jiang;Lun Li;Yimin Liu
title: Contrasting drivers of summer extreme hourly precipitation over the southeastern and northeastern Tibetan Plateau
abstract: Extreme hourly precipitation (EHP) across the Tibetan Plateau (TP) often triggers flash floods and landslides due to the region’s complex and steep terrain, yet its inter-station covariations and formation mechanisms remain inadequately understood. Using climate network analysis of hourly station data and dynamic diagnostics, this study examines EHP synchronicity across the southeastern and northeastern TP and elucidates the underlying mechanisms from a perspective of sea surface temperature (SST)-forced circulation evolution. Results show weak inter-regional synchronization of EHP occurrence between the southeastern and northeastern TP, along with an insignificant correlation in EHP frequency (EHPF) between the two subregions, indicating largely independent governing physical processes. The southeastern TP EHPF is controlled by an upper-tropospheric South Asian anticyclone and a low-level anticyclone over the Arabian Sea. The South Asian anticyclone weakens after 2000, accompanied by intensified cyclonic circulation over the northern TP. In contrast, the northeastern TP EHPF is dominated by a quasi-barotropic Northeast Asian anticyclone throughout the entire period. SST drivers of EHPF over these two subregions exhibit both regional differences and interdecadal shifts. During 1979–1999, southeastern TP EHPF is linked to an eastern North Atlantic tripole (NAT) SST anomaly pattern through a teleconnection wave train, whereas northeastern TP EHPF correlates with a western NAT configuration. After 2000, Eurasian Arctic SST anomalies emerge as dominant signals—a dipole pattern for the southeastern TP and a uniform warming pattern for the northeastern TP. These results underscore the need for region-specific EHP analysis and prediction strategies and highlight the growing role of the Arctic.

explanation: 该论文研究了数字按需服务对城市碳和物质负担的影响，特别是如何通过行为响应放大城市资源强度。虽然不直接涉及大气环境遥感技术，但与空气质量监测、城市环境分析等领域相关，因为其关注的是城市环境中的碳和物质排放问题。
topic_words: ['urban carbon', 'material and energy consumption', 'CO emissions', 'last-mile transport', 'packaging-related emissions']
authors: Fangtao Qin;Yanfei Wang;Bin Fang;Yi Wang
title: The green paradox of on-demand adaptation: how digital delivery amplifies urban carbon and material burdens
abstract: With the rapid expansion of digital on-demand services, urban residents increasingly rely on platforms as a primary adaptation to extreme heat. However, the resource implications of this shift—specifically the ‘green paradox’ where protective behavior accelerates material and energy consumption—remain poorly quantified. Drawing on transaction-level food-delivery records for 100 Chinese cities (2017–2019, 2023), we show that heat shocks trigger nonlinear surges in delivery demand, concentrated in midday peaks. By integrating these orders with a system-wide accounting of last-mile transport and packaging-related emissions, we quantify how behavioral responses propagate through urban metabolic systems. We find that delivery-related CO emissions rise more than twice as fast as demand volume, reflecting the combined influence of last-mile transport and packaging-related emissions. This elasticity gap widens in digitally dense cities with carbon-intensive grids and inefficient packaging standards. We formalize this imbalance as the Urban Green Paradox: individual heat avoidance is achieved by shifting burdens to material-intensive infrastructures. These results reveal that digital adaptation amplifies urban resource intensity under current regimes. Targeted interventions, including enforcing reusable packaging and fleet electrification, offer pathways to realign digital convenience with sustainable resource management.

explanation: 该论文研究的是2024年长江流域的极端高温热浪现象，探讨了大气环流变异性对极端热浪严重程度的影响，这与大气环境遥感技术中的大气成分分析、空气质量监测等领域密切相关。论文使用了大气环流模式分析、经验正交函数等方法，这些方法在遥感数据分析和大气环境监测中也有广泛应用。
authors: Xiao Li;Hedi Ma;Ruili Wang;Juan Zhou;Wanxin Zhang;Muyun Du;Anwei Lai;Xing Li
title: Unprecedented late-summer mega-heatwave over the Yangtze River Basin in 2024: dynamical fingerprint of extreme anomalous atmospheric circulation variability
abstract: Record-breaking heatwaves arise from the interplay between long-term warming and transient atmospheric circulation anomalies, yet the mechanisms by which atmospheric circulation variability contributes to unprecedented heatwave severity remain an active area of investigation. Here, we investigate the unprecedented late-summer 2024 super heatwave with concurrent dry conditions (LS24) over the Yangtze River Basin (YRB), which produced the largest late-summer temperature anomaly during 1979–2024. We show that the record-breaking magnitude of LS24 was primarily associated with an extreme realization of a recurrent Eurasian circulation mode superimposed on a warmer background. In the full-record Empirical Orthogonal Function analysis, the event coincided with the largest positive phase of the leading mode of late-summer Eurasian circulation variability, manifested as a trans-Eurasian Rossby wave train that established persistent East Asian ridging and a heat-dome environment over the YRB through enhanced subsidence, radiation, and moisture divergence. The constructed flow analog method partitions the 4.8 °C total anomaly into a 26%–29% long-term background, a 50%–57% circulation-associated component and a 17%–21% residual; the circulation component alone accounts for 71%–77% of the detrended anomaly. Seasonal forecast ensembles further show that the ensemble-mean response produced only modest warming and failed to reproduce the observed wave-train structure, whereas similar extreme circulation states emerged within member-to-member circulation variability and were associated with stronger YRB warming. These results highlight that, under a warming climate, rare atmospheric circulation extremes can strongly modulate regional heat severity under concurrent dry conditions and represent a fundamental challenge for seasonal prediction of unprecedented climate extremes.

explanation: 该研究使用高塔涡度协方差系统监测了中央欧洲农村地区10年的碳氧化物交换数据，涉及大气成分分析和空气质量监测，与大气环境遥感技术密切相关。
authors: László Haszpra;Zoltán Barcza;Anikó Kern;Nándor Zrinyi;Natascha Kljun
title: Long-term land-atmosphere carbon monoxide exchange from a tall tower in a rural Central European region
abstract:
The net land-atmosphere exchange of carbon monoxide remains highly uncertain due to the scarcity of long-term monitoring. This study analyses a 10-year-long data series from a tall-tower eddy covariance system. The flux footprint of this system covers a heterogeneous landscape. Vegetation-dominated areas acted as a weak net source. Solar radiation was identified as the primary driver of the emissions. Emissions from the populated areas significantly exceeded the activity-based estimations. 
 The atmospheric trace gas carbon monoxide (CO) significantly influences the atmosphere's oxidative capacity and indirectly affects climate. However, the net land-atmosphere exchange of CO remains highly uncertain due to the scarcity of long-term monitoring. This study presents and analyses a 10-year-long CO flux data series from a tall-tower eddy covariance (EC) system operated in a rural Central European region. The measured fluxes were evaluated separately for vegetation-covered, (quasi)natural areas and for populated areas. The estimated monthly mean emissions from the populated areas varied between 12 and 110 nmolm-2s-1, with the lowest value observed in July and the highest in January, respectively. The measured wintertime emissions from the populated areas significantly exceed the activity-based estimations, presumably due to underestimated emissions factors for residential heating. The vegetation-dominated sector (agricultural fields and forests) acted as a weak net CO source from April to September with an average emission of 0.58 nmolm-2s-1 (monthly range 0.31–0.91 nmolm-2s-1), with the highest value occurring in July. The diurnal peaks of the median hourly emissions can be observed around noon, and they range from 1.59 to 2.66 nmolm-2s-1. The nighttime (20:00–04:00 local standard time (LST)) hourly median values range from −1.01 to +1.17 nmolm-2s-1. Their deviations from zero are not statistically significant at a p<0.05 probability level. Solar radiation was identified as the primary driver of CO exchange. This study also demonstrates the advantages and challenges of tall-tower EC flux measurements.

explanation: 该论文研究了中国原生棕色碳气溶胶的长期演变和影响，涉及棕色碳作为一种吸收太阳短波辐射的气溶胶成分，其来源、长期趋势及其对环境和气候的影响。研究使用了化学传输模型来模拟和分析，这与大气环境遥感技术（如空气质量监测、大气成分分析）密切相关。
authors: Guochao Chen;Yiheng Wang;Qi Ying;Xiaofei Wang;Hongliang Zhang
title: Long-term evolution and effects of primary brown carbon aerosol in China
abstract:
Brown carbon (BrC) aerosols absorb solar shortwave radiation and affect the environment and climate. Using a chemical transport model, we investigated the sources and long-term trends of primary BrC in China. Residential and industrial emissions dominate primary BrC in China, unlike the global pattern. Anthropogenic BrC accounts for most of the direct radiative effects and responds significantly to emission changes, indicating potential climate benefits of emission control measures. 
 Brown carbon (BrC) is a light-absorbing component of organic aerosols that influences atmospheric environment and climate. Although biomass burning is recognized as the major source of primary BrC (PBrC) globally, anthropogenic sources can contribute comparably or more to PBrC in regions with intensive human activities, yet variations in concentrations and effects of PBrC remain underexplored in China, where dramatic emission changes occurred in last two decades.We apply an internal mixing model to simulate the long-term (2005–2020) variations of PBrC surface and vertical concentrations and their effects across China. The mean surface PBrC concentration is 0.81 µgC m−3, with anthropogenic emissions dominating: residential, industrial combustion, and agricultural sectors contribute on average 57 %, 22 %, and 18 %, respectively, together accounting for 91 % of column concentrations in 2010. PBrC (−20.8 %) declined more than PM2.5 (−8.1 %), accompanied by a slight reduction in O3 and a decrease in direct radiative effect (DRE) from +0.032 W m−2 in 2005 to +0.023 W m−2 in 2020 (−25.7 %), with anthropogenic sources contributing 84.2 % of total DRE.This study provides the first long-term assessment of PBrC trends, sources, and radiative effects in human-dominated regions, demonstrating that emission controls can deliver both environment and climate co-benefits.

explanation: 该论文使用卫星和地面观测数据评估欧洲国家的甲烷排放，涉及卫星观测技术和大气成分分析，与大气环境遥感技术密切相关。
authors: Shuai Sun;Yuzhong Zhang;Wei Chen;Shaomin Pan;Dongchuan Pu;Xin Tong;Huilin Chen;Sander Houweling
title: Assessment of methane emissions from European countries using satellite and surface observations
abstract:
This study estimates methane emissions across Europe from 2019 to 2023 using atmospheric methane measurements from satellites and ground stations to improve understanding of emission sources. We find that total emissions are slightly higher than official reports, mainly due to livestock and waste, while emissions from fossil fuel production are lower in some regions. These results show that atmospheric measurements can improve independent verification of emissions and support climate policy. 
 Europe is a global leader in mitigating methane emissions through comprehensive policies, including the EU Methane Strategy and commitments under the Global Methane Pledge. National bottom-up inventories are widely regarded as high quality; however, atmospheric observations remain essential for independent verification and tracking emission reductions. Here, we present a multi-year (2019–2023) top-down assessment of European methane emissions using a Bayesian inversion of satellite observations from TROPOMI and surface measurements from ICOS. Analysis of observational constraints shows that surface measurements provide the dominant information, while satellite observations offer complementary coverage in regions not covered by the surface network. The inversion estimates total European methane emissions at 25.7 Tg yr−1, including 22.5 Tg yr−1 from anthropogenic sources, which is 1.0 Tg yr−1 higher than the prior inventory. The upward adjustments are likely associated with livestock and waste emissions in central and western Europe, partly offset by lower fossil fuel emissions in the North Sea. National emissions for the Netherlands, Germany, and Italy are 18 %–80 % higher than the values reported to the UNFCCC. The inversion also reveals an overall decline in anthropogenic emissions, with a linear trend of −0.25 Tg yr−2. While consistent in magnitude with the prior estimate, the inversion shows a distinct spatial pattern: increases in livestock and waste emissions in western Europe contrast with decreases in fossil fuel production regions such as the North Sea and Poland. These findings highlight the value of atmospheric observations for evaluating methane inventories and informing climate policy.

explanation: 该论文研究了印度河-恒河平原的离子和粒子尺寸分布，重点关注新粒子形成事件，这与大气环境遥感技术（如空气质量监测和大气成分分析）密切相关。论文涉及粒子形成、大气成分和气溶胶检索等主题，直接关联到遥感技术在环境监测中的应用。
topic_words: ['New particle formation', 'atmospheric composition', 'aerosol retrieval', 'Indo-Gangetic Plain', 'ion measurements']
authors: Gaurav Kumar Srivastav;Aasif Ahmad Wagay;Janne Lampilahti;Jaswant Rathore;Ravi Kumar Kunchala;Dilip Ganguly;Markku Kulmala;Tuukka Petäjä;Pauli Paasonen;Roseline C. Thakur;Shahzad Gani
title: Ion and particle size distribution measurements in the Indo-Gangetic Plain: seasonal insights and challenges in new particle formation event characterization
abstract:
Particle formation events affect climate and air quality. Using measurements of particle number concentrations down to very small particles (~3 nm) in polluted northern India, we show that these events occur frequently in summer under reduced background particle load. However, in this environment, emissions and changing air masses can mask or distort these events, making them difficult to detect. Such environments require adaptation of standard analytical methods used in cleaner regions. 
 New particle formation (NPF) is a major source of atmospheric aerosols and cloud condensation nuclei, influencing climate and air quality. In highly polluted regions such as the Indo-Gangetic Plain (IGP), where precursor concentrations and condensation sinks are among the highest globally, NPF remains poorly constrained due to limited observations of particles and ions in the sub–10 nm size range.Here, we investigated the occurrence and growth of NPF at a suburban IGP site (CAS-AO, Sonipat, Haryana), during May–December 2023 using ion (0.8–42 nm) and particle (2.5–42 nm) measurements together with meteorological data. NPF events were frequent during summer, occurring on 30 of 35 valid days in May–June (86 %), and were much less frequent during the winter/post-monsoon period, with 20 out of 73 valid days (28 %). The weak seasonal variability of ion concentrations relative to nucleation-mode particles suggests that particle survival and growth were strongly modulated by condensation sink, meteorology, and air-mass heterogeneity. The median daily condensation sink during 06:00–12:00 LT was lower on event days than on non-event days (0.0095 vs. 0.0292 s−1). Particle growth rates increased with size, from 14.7 nm h−1 in the 3–7 nm range to 19.0 nm h−1 in the 7–20 nm range, indicating size-dependent growth.In this high-background setting, pollution plumes and meteorological variability intermittently mask or distort NPF signals, limiting the direct applicability of both visual and automated classification methods and growth rate estimation methods. Our observations highlight that careful application and improvement of data analysis methods, along with precursor gas measurements, are required to better constrain nucleation processes by avoiding methodological sensitivity due to the complexity of aerosol dynamic processes in multi-source, high-condensation-sink environments, such as IGP.

explanation: 该论文研究了大西洋环流减弱对气溶胶、云层和辐射的影响，涉及气溶胶-云相互作用、萨赫勒尘等，与大气环境遥感技术（如空气质量监测、卫星观测、大气成分分析、气溶胶反演）密切相关。
authors: Ryan Vella;Ulrike Lohmann
title: Aerosol–cloud interactions influence the  climate response to AMOC weakening
abstract:
The Atlantic overturning circulation carries heat northward and may weaken with climate change. We show that this can redistribute natural aerosols, especially Saharan dust, altering clouds and producing strong regional effects over the North Atlantic. Globally, cloud changes largely cancel out, leaving a small warming effect, whereas increased sea ice, snow, and dust produce an overall cooling. 
 The Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC) strongly influences regional climate, yet how atmospheric aerosols and aerosol–cloud interactions respond to its weakening remains largely unexplored. Using an aerosol-climate model, we examine how a 60 % AMOC weakening affects aerosols, clouds, and radiation. The weakening drives a hemispheric aerosol redistribution through purely dynamical pathways, increasing the Northern Hemisphere aerosol burden by 41 % through enhanced Saharan dust emissions and longer lifetimes under suppressed wet deposition. Averaged over 40–90° N, in-cloud droplet number increases by 10 % in warm clouds and 11 % in mixed-phase clouds, while enhanced dust ice-nucleating particles raise mixed-phase ice crystal number by 32 %, promoting the Wegener–Bergeron–Findeisen process and reducing mixed-phase total water path by 8 %. A kernel decomposition shows substantial regional cloud radiative responses, particularly over the North Atlantic, but opposing contributions largely cancel in the global mean, leaving a small net cloud radiative response of +0.21Wm-2. This near cancellation reflects subpolar low-cloud brightening offset by optical thinning of mixed-phase and ice clouds, partly driven by dust-induced glaciation, together with opposing tropical cloud changes from the southward ITCZ shift. This small global mean cloud contribution contrasts with previous studies of AMOC weakening, in which cloud changes contribute a net positive radiative feedback on the surface response. Of the cloud, aerosol and surface-albedo contributions diagnosed here, the largest effect comes from the enhanced shortwave reflection by expanded sea-ice and snow cover (−0.83 W m−2), followed by the effective radiative forcing due to dust aerosol–radiation interactions (ERFari, −0.23 W m−2). Combined with the cloud contribution, these terms sum to −0.86 W m−2. This estimate excludes the longwave response to the cooling, including the Planck and lapse-rate responses, which is not decomposed here.

explanation: 该论文研究了海盐气溶胶对海洋低云中暖雨形成的影响，涉及大气环境中的气溶胶（海盐颗粒）和云降水过程，这与大气环境遥感技术（如空气质量监测、卫星观测、大气成分分析、气溶胶反演）密切相关，因此是强相关的。
authors: Katherine Mifsud;Jason Barr;Robert Wood;Yonghoon Choi;Ewan Crosbie;Glenn S. Diskin;Joshua P. DiGangi;Richard H. Moore;Claire Robinson;Michael A. Shook;Armin Sorooshian;Christiane Voigt;Luke Ziemba
title: Coarse-mode sea spray aerosols enhance warm rain formation in marine low clouds
abstract:
Salt particles from the ocean can help marine clouds precipitate more quickly, but their role is not fully understood. Using aircraft observations over the northwest Atlantic Ocean and computer simulations, we studied how these particles affect warm rain formation. We found that clouds containing more large sea salt particles, even at relatively low amounts, produce more rain. These results improve understanding of how sea salt aerosols influence clouds, rainfall, and climate. 
 Precipitation in low clouds affects cloud responses to aerosol perturbations, thereby impacting aerosol radiative forcing of climate, a significant but indeterminate contribution to uncertainty in future warming. The onset of drizzle formation in marine low clouds may be influenced by the presence of supermicron sea salt aerosols. These particles can act as giant CCN (GCCN) that benefit from rapid condensational growth to a size that initiates collision-coalescence. Aircraft-based in-situ observations of cloud microphysical properties and aerosol size distributions from the Aerosol Cloud meTeorology Interactions oVer the western ATlantic Experiment (ACTIVATE) are analyzed from January–June 2022. Observations from a cloud aerosol spectrometer and a cloud droplet probe in clear air are used to quantify GCCN size distributions. Modest correlations are found between GCCN and near surface-level wind speeds when averaged together into wind speed bins, a result consistent with other studies. Observed GCCN distributions and cloud thicknesses are used to drive simulations within a 1-dimensional kinematic super droplet model, exploring the conditions under which the observed GCCN distributions induce a first-order impact on precipitation rate. The model demonstrates that even relatively small GCCN salt masses (∼ 1 µg m−3) can accelerate the onset of drizzle in lightly precipitating marine low clouds. Similarly, a statistical analysis of in-cloud data shows the ratio of rainwater to total condensed water is higher when GCCN concentration/mass is above average. Together, the results indicate a significant influence of GCCN on precipitation formation in marine low clouds.

explanation: 该论文研究了中高层大气中的准26天波，使用了地面观测和卫星测量数据，涉及大气温度和成分的遥感技术，与大气环境遥感技术密切相关。
authors: Christoph Kalicinsky;Sandra Wallis;Lukas Depenthal;Christoph G. Hoffmann;Anna Lange;Christian von Savigny
title: Simultaneous ground-based observations of a large quasi 26 d wave from three different measurement sites in northern mid-latitudes
abstract:
We present simultaneous observations of a planetary 26-day wave in mesospheric temperature observed by three different ground-based mid-latitude OH spectrometers at stations in Germany in boreal winter 2016/2017. With supporting information from satellite measurements the event can be linked to a Rossby wave (1,4) mode. The periodic changes are also seen in other atmospheric parameters such as atomic oxygen further illustrating the importance of such events for the atmospheric state. 
 We present simultaneous observations of a remarkable planetary wave event in mesospheric temperature observed by three different ground-based mid-latitude OH spectrometers at stations in Germany (Greifswald (54° N, 13° E), Wuppertal (51° N, 7° E), and Hohenpeißenberg (48° N, 11° E)) during boreal winter 2016/2017. Additionally, temperature profile observations with the satellite instruments SABER/TIMED and MLS/Aura are used for supporting information on the global distribution of the wave event.The observed wave had a period of about 26 d and an amplitude of partly up to about 20 K. The satellite temperature observations confirmed that the wave signature exhibited all the characteristics of the well known Rossby (1,4) normal mode oscillation. To the best of our knowledge this is the first study reporting on such a strong Rossby (1,4) wave in the middle atmosphere of the Northern Hemisphere. The wave signature was also identified in atomic oxygen mixing ratios in the mesopause region and lower thermosphere observed with SABER illustrating the importance of such wave events not only for the temperature distribution but also for the temporal variation of trace-gas distributions.

explanation: 该论文研究液滴冻结实验，这些实验有助于研究大气中引发冰形成的物质。虽然论文主要关注统计学方法（如Kaplan-Meier置信区间和曲线比较），但其研究对象与大气环境（如冰核形成、大气成分分析）密切相关，因此与大气环境遥感技术相关。
authors: Thomas F. Whale;Trystan Surawy-Stepney;Sarah L. Barr
title: Survival-analysis methods for droplet-freezing data: Kaplan–Meier confidence intervals and non-parametric curve comparison
abstract:
Droplet-freezing experiments help us study substances that trigger ice formation in the atmosphere, but existing ways to show uncertainty or compare results are lacking. We adapt confidence intervals used in medical time-to-even studies, then test them using realistic simulations. They work well across most of the freezing range, though less well at its limits. We also compare tests for differences between curves and show that the best choice depends on how the curves differ. 
 Droplet-freezing assays underpin immersion-mode ice-nucleation research yet approaches to uncertainty quantification for fraction-frozen curves and derived active-site densities (ns(T)) are inconsistent. Further, there is currently no rigorous method for significance testing the difference between fraction-frozen curves. To address these issues, we recast droplet-freezing measurements as survival data and apply analysis techniques typically used in medical statistics. Using the Kaplan–Meier estimator, we derive nonparametric pointwise confidence intervals for droplet fraction-frozen without binning or model assumptions. These intervals can also be propagated to cumulative ice-nucleation activity spectra such as  K(T), ns(T) or nm(T). Simulations based on fitted literature freezing curves show that Kaplan–Meier intervals have close to nominal coverage over the central portion of fraction-frozen curves, but coverage deteriorates near the ends of the curve where finite experiments contain little information. We also compare several statistical tests for distinguishing between droplet-freezing curves. These tests quantify whether the observed separation between two finite-droplet curves is larger than expected from sampling variability alone. The log-rank test, often used alongside Kaplan–Meier confidence intervals in medical statistics, can be useful for approximately proportional-hazards-like alternatives, but can have low power when curves differ in shape or reflect multiple ice-active populations. We therefore introduce an integrated squared fraction-frozen distance permutation test, which we refer to as the Integrated Squared Difference (ISD) test. This test compares the accumulated squared separation between two empirical fraction-frozen curves directly and does not require proportional hazards. Simulations comparing the ISD test, log-rank and several standard empirical-distribution-function tests show that no single test is most powerful in all situations: performance depends on droplet number, curve shape, and the form of the difference being tested. We recommend reporting fraction-frozen curves with Kaplan–Meier pointwise confidence intervals and droplet numbers, and using the ISD test for general curve comparison. We note finally that a significant global test indicates that two curves differ somewhere over the analysed temperature interval, but does not identify where they differ or why; this still requires inspection of the curves and potentially of normalised spectra.

explanation: 该论文与大气环境遥感技术密切相关，因为它研究的是从历史观测站获取的大气电场数据，这些数据对于分析大气成分、气候变化以及全球电电路等环境问题至关重要。虽然论文主要关注历史数据数字化，但其研究内容（大气电场、潜在梯度等）直接涉及大气环境遥感领域。
topic_words: ['atmospheric electric field', 'potential gradient', 'global electric circuit', 'climate variability', 'citizen science']
authors: Hripsime Mkrtchyan;Keri A. Nicoll;R. Giles Harrison;Anna Hovhannisyan
title: Digitization of Historical Atmospheric Electricity Records from Lerwick Observatory (1927–1956) using Citizen Science
abstract:
This paper presents the rescue of thirty years of handwritten atmospheric electric field records from a remote Lerwick observatory in Shetland. Nearly two thousand volunteers helped read and digitize the old paper sheets online. The result is a rare, long-term dataset showing how atmospheric electricity changes through the day and across seasons, supporting future climate research and showing how public participation can bring forgotten historical data back to life. 
 Measurements of the atmospheric electric field, measured as the potential gradient (PG), were carried out at Lerwick Observatory (Shetland Isles, UK) during the twentieth century and provide a unique resource for studying links between atmospheric electricity, the global electric circuit (GEC), and climate variability. Most of these historical observations existed previously only as handwritten or printed records, limiting their accessibility for modern analysis. A comprehensive digitization of the Lerwick PG handwritten records from 1927–1956 has been undertaken using a citizen science approach, through the Zooniverse platform. The resulting ready-to-use dataset provides a quality-controlled record of hourly potential gradient measurements, enabling new investigations into long-term atmospheric electricity variability, the global electric circuit, and their associated connections to climate. In addition, seasonal variability analysed on an hourly basis across the entire observation period is presented for the first time.

explanation: 该论文研究了绿色屋顶对城市热岛效应的影响，并使用WRF模型进行模拟和评估。绿色屋顶的模拟涉及大气与地表的能量和水分交换，这与大气环境遥感技术（如城市热岛监测、地表能量平衡分析）密切相关。因此，该论文与大气环境遥感技术有较强的关联。
authors: Alireza Saeedi;Maria Martinez Mendoza;Eric Scott Krayenhoff;James Voogt;Hang Yin;Andrea Zonato;Sylvie Leroyer;Claudia Wagner-Riddle
title: Process-based upgrades to the WRF multi-layer green-roof scheme (WRF-MLGR v2.0) and evaluation against field observations
abstract:
Green roofs can help cool hot cities, and the Weather Research and Forecasting model lets us test how much. We upgraded its multi-layer green-roof scheme, adding plant shading, realistic heat flow in wet soil, evaporation from soil and wet leaves, and water uptake from deeper soil. Tested on a green roof in London, Canada, the new scheme cut errors in heat entering the roof by about three-quarters and captured bursts of evaporation after rain, improving how we study green-roof cooling. 
 Green roofs can moderate urban heat by increasing latent heat flux and reducing sensible heat flux. However, capturing these effects in models depends on accurate representation of key green-roof processes, including substrate heat and moisture transport, soil-vegetation-atmosphere energy and moisture exchanges, interactions with the underlying roof, and drainage. Here we introduce targeted, process-based updates to the green-roof scheme (hereafter, MLGR) within the multi-layer urban canopy model (BEP-BEM) in the WRF mesoscale model to address key limitations in the original formulation. The updates include a non-linear dependence of soil thermal conductivity on moisture, vegetation-modulated surface thermal conductivity, explicit soil-surface evaporation, multi-layer root water uptake for transpiration, and canopy interception with evaporation and dew formation. We evaluate the original and modified MLGR schemes using hourly observations from an extensive sedum roof in London, Canada, for “summer” (1 July–31 August 2014) and “fall” (1 September–31 October 2014) periods. We also analyze 11–18 October 2025, when green roof modules were placed directly on the roof deck – which corresponds to the model's lower boundary assumption. Following implementation of the process-based improvements, model–measurement agreement for the conductive heat flux is markedly improved: RMSE is reduced from 105.9 to 24.0 W m−2 in summer and from 94.2 to 24.0 W m−2 in fall and the model produces more realistic overall green roof energy partitioning. The modified model better captures post-rain increases in latent heat flux (QE) and improves the timing and magnitude of daytime turbulent latent and sensible heat flux peaks (QE and QH). Drainage is reduced relative to the original scheme; however, it remains slightly underestimated during summer and slightly overestimated during fall, and biases persist in surface temperature (warm during the day and cool at night) and in the magnitude and variability of QE. Overall, the revised MLGR physics improves surface-flux realism, and future development should focus on developing a more realistic vegetation canopy submodule.

explanation: 该论文研究了南半球平流层的环流及其与热带风、臭氧和Hunga喷发的关系，涉及大气成分分析和动力学，与大气环境遥感技术密切相关。
authors: Xinyue Wang;Wandi Yu;William Randel;Rolando Garcia;Paul Newman;Simone Tilmes;Ewa Bednarz;Yunqian Zhu;Jun Zhang;V. Lynn Harvey;Simchan Yook;Chengyun Yang;Zhihong Zhuo
title: Stratospheric Circulation in the Southern Hemisphere: Links to Tropical Winds, Ozone and the Hunga Eruption—Part II: Evidence From a Global Chemistry‐Climate Model
abstract: The Southern Hemisphere (SH) stratospheric circulation can be categorized based upon the development of a Low‐Latitude Jet (LLJ) in the upper stratosphere during winter months. We analyze the dynamics of the LLJ based on a large ensemble of chemistry‐climate model simulations, supported by reanalysis data. The LLJ is associated with westerly wind anomalies in the middle and upper stratosphere during mid‐winter, coupled with weak planetary wave activity and a slower Brewer‐Dobson circulation. Circulation effects extend into the tropical upper stratosphere, where the LLJ impacts the tropical semi‐annual oscillation (SAO). Additionally, the LLJ is linked to a persistent, strong polar vortex in the lower stratosphere during October–December. This cold, strong vortex is associated with decreased ozone amounts in winter and spring; ozone radiative feedbacks reinforce the cold polar vortex after sunlight returns in October. The 2022 Hunga eruption coincided with an anomalously strong LLJ year, and ensemble simulations show that the Hunga eruption shifted the SH winter circulation toward the LLJ state, although the ensemble‐mean forced Hunga signal is small compared with the observed 2022 anomalies and is embedded within a large amount of stochastic variability. These results establish the LLJ as a robust mode of SH winter stratospheric variability and provide a new insight for interpreting the dynamical response to the Hunga eruption in the context of natural variability.

authors: Wandi Yu;Xinyue Wang;William J. Randel;Rolando R. Garcia;Paul A. Newman;Sean Davis;Karen H. Rosenlof
title: Stratospheric Circulation in the Southern Hemisphere: Links to Tropical Winds, Ozone, and the Hunga Eruption—Part 1: Evidence From ERA5 Reanalysis
abstract: The interannual variability of the Southern Hemisphere polar vortex plays a key role in ozone depletion and recovery but this variability and its teleconnection patterns are less understood than in the Northern Hemisphere. Using ERA5 reanalysis data from 1980 to 2022 (43 years), we studied the variability of the Southern Hemisphere vortex by focusing on the location of the winter jet maximum in the upper stratosphere (1 hPa). We identify two dominant modes: In the first one, the core of the jet at 1 hPa remains at lower latitudes (40°S–50°S, LLJ) throughout austral winter (9 years, including 2022 following the Hunga eruption). In the second mode, the core of the jet shifts poleward (60°S–70°S, HLJ) in mid‐July and stays at high latitudes throughout August (15 years, including the 2002 and 2019 sudden warming events). In the remaining 19 years, the jet does not fall into either of these modes. LLJ years are linked to weaker upward propagating wave activity near the tropopause and a planetary wave index of refraction that inhibits propagation in the stratosphere; these years also have a stronger, colder polar vortex and greater ozone depletion during late winter and spring. HLJ years show the opposite behavior. Observations suggests a link with the Quasi‐Biennial Oscillation: LLJ years often occur when tropical westerlies are present at 10 hPa; HLJ years occur when tropical easterlies are present at that level. These findings suggest the latitude of the upper stratospheric jet provides a useful diagnostic for understanding Southern Hemisphere stratospheric dynamics.

explanation: 该论文研究了低热层大气潮的时空变化及其与ENSO、QBO、PJO、MJO和Lyα辐射的关系，涉及大气环境监测和空间天气，与大气环境遥感技术（如卫星观测、大气成分分析）密切相关。
authors: Yosuke Yamazaki;Huixin Liu;Kaoru Sato;Dai Koshin;Claudia Stolle
title: Tidal Variability in the Lower Thermosphere: Relative Importance of ENSO, QBO, PJO, MJO, and Lyα
abstract: Atmospheric tides in the lower thermosphere play an important role in regulating upper‐atmospheric conditions relevant to space weather. However, their spatial and temporal variability remains poorly understood, apart from seasonal variations. Previous studies have shown that tides can be influenced by meteorological and solar conditions. This study clarifies the relative importance of the El Niño‐Southern Oscillation (ENSO), the Quasi‐Biennial Oscillation (QBO), the Northern and Southern Polar‐night Jet Oscillations (NPJO and SPJO), the Madden‐Julian Oscillation (MJO), and Lyman‐alpha (Lyα $\alpha $) radiation to tidal variability in the lower thermosphere. Tides at 80–110 km are derived from hourly temperature and wind fields in the JAGUAR‐DAS Whole neutral Atmosphere Reanalysis (JAWARA) for the period September 2004–August 2025. Rotated empirical orthogonal function analysis is used to identify the dominant modes of de‐seasonalized tidal variability. The resulting principal component time series are used as daily indices of tidal activity and are compared with indices of ENSO, QBO, NPJO, SPJO, MJO, and Lyα $\alpha $. Multiple linear regression analysis determines which tides exhibit statistically significant responses to these indices and quantifies their magnitudes. The most pronounced responses include those of the nonmigrating diurnal tide DE3 to ENSO (approximately ± $\pm $4 m s−1 ${\mathrm{s}}^{-1}$ in horizontal wind velocity), the migrating diurnal tide DW1 to QBO (∼± $\pm $10 m s−1 ${\mathrm{s}}^{-1}$), and the migrating semidiurnal tide SW2 to NPJO (∼± $\pm $12 m s−1 ${\mathrm{s}}^{-1}$) and SPJO (∼± $\pm $7 m s−1 ${\mathrm{s}}^{-1}$). Tidal responses to MJO and Lyα $\alpha $ are relatively weak and are therefore not identified with the same level of confidence.

title: Methane Emissions in Melbourne, Australia. Part 2: Improving Prior Estimates Using Synthesis Inversion
abstract: Urban methane emissions remain highly uncertain due to the complexity of overlapping anthropogenic sources and limitations in current bottom‐up inventories. In this study, we apply a synthesis inversion framework to refine sector‐specific methane emissions for the Melbourne region in Australia, using in situ atmospheric observations and a Bayesian inversion approach. Our method incorporates constrained and unconstrained inversions, observational filtering, and ensemble‐based uncertainty quantification, including both ensemble spread and posterior covariance structure. The inversion indicates that prior methane emissions are substantially underestimated, particularly for emissions from gas infrastructure, which are inferred to be approximately five to seven times larger than prior estimates. Posterior emission estimates show substantial improvements in agreement with observations, as evidenced by reduced root mean square error (RMSE), increased correlation, and lower model bias across five receptor sites. Posterior methane emissions for the Melbourne region range from 222 to 253 kt/year across the six study months, representing a 67%–90% increase relative to the prior inventory of 133.5 kt/year. Sensitivity analyses confirm that these total emission estimates are robust to prior perturbations and inversion configuration choices. However, source attribution remains sensitive in cases of spatial overlap or low observational coverage. This study demonstrates the effectiveness of synthesis inversion in urban methane quantification and highlights its value for supporting targeted mitigation strategies and improving emission reporting in urban Australia.

title: 3D Atmospheric Imprint of Mesoscale Eddies Driven by the Thermal Feedback in the Gulf Stream Region
abstract: The 3D imprint of mesoscale ocean eddies on the overlying atmosphere is investigated using coupled ocean‐atmosphere high‐resolution simulation of the Gulf Stream region, distinguishing cyclones and anticyclones. Sea surface temperature (SST) anomalies are predominantly warm for anticyclones and cold for cyclones, driving a Thermal Feedback (TFB) to the atmosphere. Wind‐rotated eddy composites method reveals significant modulation by eddies in wind speed, planetary boundary layer height (PBLH), cloud cover and vertical velocities. However, no significant precipitation anomalies are retrieved. The wind derivatives reveal different vertical scales: wind curl anomalies extend straight above the eddies up to about 600 m, while wind divergence anomalies are significant only in near‐surface. Furthermore, vertical velocity anomalies extend up to twice above the mean PBLH. The TFB impacts significantly the wind speed, wind divergence, PBLH and vertical wind anomalies, through downward‐momentum mixing and pressure adjustment processes. It has a top‐down effect: the planetary boundary layer (PBL) stability is affected by the heat fluxes anomalies driven by the TFB directly above the eddy. Planetary boundary layer height modulation further goes along vertical velocities and wind divergence in near‐surface, lagged downstream of the eddy by about 2–3 hr, suggesting important non‐local ocean‐atmosphere coupling impacts. The coupling of PBLH modulation to SST anomalies is about +40mK−1 ${+}40\,\mathrm{m}\,{\mathrm{K}}^{-\mathrm{1}}$, about 30% lower than previous studies using coarser resolution simulations that consider only large eddies. This suggests the PBLH response to mesoscale eddies was overestimated due to poor representation of smaller eddies.

title: Methane Emissions in Melbourne, Australia; Part 1: Prior Estimates Using Global and National Data
abstract: This paper is the first part of a comprehensive study that enhances the understanding of methane emissions in Melbourne, Australia, by combining emission inventories and atmospheric observations. We utilized global, national and regional datasets to produce prior gridded estimates of methane emissions for the Melbourne region. We ran an atmospheric transport model with these prior emissions and boundary conditions from the Whole Atmosphere Community Climate Model (WACCM), and compared the calculated mole fractions with observations at five stations during January to June 2023. Our comparisons revealed a mismatch in the boundary conditions from WACCM and the long‐term national baseline data. We adjusted the boundary condition information using long‐term in situ observations, which significantly reduced a nearly 50 ppb offset in the global boundary condition data. Our results indicate that the model driven by prior emission estimates reproduces the observed temporal variability of atmospheric methane reasonably well, but systematically underestimates mole fraction magnitudes. We see biases for each month and site of approximately 20–196 ppb without data selection, reducing to about 5–52 ppb when nighttime low wind‐speed data are excluded. This suggests that the prior methane emissions are underestimated in the Melbourne region.

authors: Yaqi Zhao;Jun Liu;Huiying Xuan;Yonghong Wang;Biwu Chu;Yongcheng Jia;Tianzeng Chen;Xu Sun;Qingxin Ma;Hong He
title: Distinct Role of NH3 in Enhancing Atmospheric Nitrous Acid Formation: Evidence From an Autumn Field Campaign in Beijing
abstract: Nitrous acid (HONO) is a key precursor of hydroxyl radicals (·OH), which plays a central role in atmospheric oxidation and aerosol formation. However, the mechanisms responsible for frequently elevated HONO levels, particularly the role of ammonia (NH3) under complex atmospheric pollution conditions, remain under debate. Here, simultaneous measurements of HONO, NH3, and related atmospheric parameters were conducted in downtown Beijing during autumn 2021. A comprehensive HONO budget analysis combined with a residual based approach was applied to decouple the influence of relative humidity (RH) and isolate the contribution of NH3. The results indicate that known sources explain about 75% of the observed HONO, implying a substantial missing source (Punknown) during the daytime and nighttime. Crucially, we provide observational evidence that NH3 enhances HONO formation through distinct mechanisms both during nighttime and daytime. At night, HONO production efficiency after RH correction increased with NH3 concentration, indicating that NH3 independently facilitates heterogeneous NO2 hydrolysis by neutralizing surface acidity. During the daytime, however, HONO production showed a pronounced contribution from particulate nitrate photolysis, with NH3 indirectly promoting HONO via enhanced nitrate formation. Notably, this NH3 driven enhancement of HONO production was profound even during relatively clean periods: elevated NH3 levels (≥10 ppb) increased HONO derived ·OH production by 83%, significantly accelerating atmospheric oxidation cycles. These findings highlight NH3 as a regulator of atmospheric oxidation capacity, suggesting that synergetic control of NH3 is essential for mitigating surface ozone pollution given the remarkable role of HONO in ozone formation in megacities.

title: Weakened Variability of Afro‐Asian Monsoonal Precipitation in Response to a Past Warm‐Cold Transition
abstract: The Afro‐Asian monsoon domain faces a “wetter and more variable” paradigm under future warming, but whether a “drier and less variable” hydroclimate emerges under cooling remains unconstrained. Using a ∼1° transient global climate simulation during the Last Interglacial (130–115 ka) covering the precession‐induced warm‐cold transition, we demonstrate a general weakening trend of precipitation variability over the Afro‐Asian monsoon domain except for southern India at multiple timescales, but with divergent dynamical mechanisms. Precipitation variability changes are dynamically dominated by the vertical motion variability over the Asian monsoon domain associated with diabatic heating, while thermodynamically controlled by cooling‐induced reduced atmospheric moisture over West Africa. Furthermore, we found no fixed relationship between changes in mean precipitation and its variability across the Afro‐Asian monsoon zone during the warm‐cold transition due to their distinct driving mechanisms, contrasting to the uniformly thermodynamic‐driven variability in greenhouse gas‐induced warmer world. Despite the discrepant external forcings between the seasonally/latitudinal‐dependent Earth's orbit across the Last Interglacial and the uniform year‐round greenhouse‐gas, our findings reveal how precipitation variability responses under contrasting climate states. These results offer insights into how gradual long‐term orbital forcing regulate short‐term precipitation variability.

title: Temperature Dependence of O2 Collision‐Induced Absorption Near 1.06 μm Measured by Cavity Ring‐Down Spectroscopy
abstract: Oxygen collision‐induced absorption (CIA) near 1.06μm $1.06\,{\upmu }\mathrm{m}$ is extremely weak, yet accurate spectroscopic data for this band are important for atmospheric radiative‐transfer modeling and the interpretation of oxygen‐rich planetary atmospheres. This spectral region contains narrow O2 monomer absorption lines arising from the a1Δgv′=1←X3Σg−v″=0 ${a}^{1}{{\Delta }}_{g}\left({v}^{\prime }=1\right){\leftarrow}{X}^{3}{{\Sigma }}_{g}^{-}\left({v}^{{\prime\prime}}=0\right)$ transition, superimposed on broad oxygen CIA. In this work, cavity ring‐down spectroscopy was used to measure O2–O2 CIA over 9120–9820cm−1 $9820\,\mathrm{c}{\mathrm{m}}^{-\mathrm{1}}$ at 273, 303, and 333 K under low‐density conditions (<1amagat) $(<  1\,\mathrm{a}\mathrm{m}\mathrm{a}\mathrm{g}\mathrm{a}\mathrm{t})$. The three pressure data sets recorded at 303 K gave mutually consistent BO2−O2 ${B}_{{\mathrm{O}}_{\mathrm{2}}-{\mathrm{O}}_{\mathrm{2}}}$ spectra, with deviations mostly below 0.3% within the FWHM range of 9301–9502cm−1 $9502\,\mathrm{c}{\mathrm{m}}^{-\mathrm{1}}$. Linear fitting of the BO2−O2 ${B}_{{\mathrm{O}}_{\mathrm{2}}-{\mathrm{O}}_{\mathrm{2}}}$ values at the three temperatures yielded temperature‐dependence coefficients, (dB/dT)ν ${(dB/dT)}_{\nu }$, which are predominantly positive and indicate an overall enhancement of O2–O2 CIA in this band with increasing temperature. Comparison with the ab initio data shows that both experiment and theory predict a positive temperature dependence. However, over the common integration interval of 9120–9660cm−1 $9660\,\mathrm{c}{\mathrm{m}}^{-\mathrm{1}}$, the experimental temperature‐dependence coefficient of the integrated band intensity, dS/dT $dS/dT$, is 4.13(14)×10−7cm−2amagat−2K−1 $4.13(14)\times 1{0}^{-7}\,\mathrm{c}{\mathrm{m}}^{-\mathrm{2}}\,\mathrm{a}\mathrm{m}\mathrm{a}\mathrm{g}\mathrm{a}{\mathrm{t}}^{-\mathrm{2}}\,{\mathrm{K}}^{-\mathrm{1}}$, smaller than the theoretical value of 5.49×10−7cm−2amagat−2K−1 $5.49\times 1{0}^{-7}\,\mathrm{c}{\mathrm{m}}^{-\mathrm{2}}\,\mathrm{a}\mathrm{m}\mathrm{a}\mathrm{g}\mathrm{a}{\mathrm{t}}^{-\mathrm{2}}\,{\mathrm{K}}^{-\mathrm{1}}$. These results provide new experimental constraints on the temperature dependence of O2–O2 CIA near 1.06μm $1.06\,{\upmu }\mathrm{m}$ and support the evaluation and refinement of theoretical descriptions of this band.

title: An in situ forming immunomodulatory hydrogel reinvigorates exhausted CD8+ T cells via preserving their mitochondrial fitness
abstract: CD8+T cell exhaustion driven by mitochondrial dysfunction remains a major barrier to effective cancer immunotherapy. Here, we report an in situ formingd-α-tocopheryl polyethylene glycol succinate (TPGS)–based hydrogel [multifunctional thermosensitive composite gel (MTC Gel)] that reinvigorates exhausted CD8+T cells by preserving mitochondrial fitness through a two-pronged strategy. After intratumoral injection, MTC Gel rapidly undergoes gelation at physiological temperature and dissociates to generate a high local concentration of TPGS, which targets cancer cell mitochondria to trigger prodeath mitophagy. This process induces robust immunogenic cell death (ICD) and blocks tunneling nanotube–mediated mitochondrial hijacking. Meanwhile, NLG919-loaded hybrid nanoparticles released from MTC Gel synergistically restore mitochondrial biogenesis in CD8+T cells suppressed by indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase 1. Across multiple murine tumor models, MTC Gel reprograms T cell immunity by reducing CD8+T cells exhaustion while enhancing effector and cytotoxic functions, thereby eliciting potent tumoricidal activity. These findings highlight this rationally designed hydrogel system as a clinically translatable platform for next-generation ICD-based cancer immunotherapies.

title: NRF2 coordinates cystine import and glutathione use to sustain ferroptosis resistance and formaldehyde tolerance in cancer
abstract: Cancer cells must balance detoxification of reactive metabolic by-products while preserving redox homeostasis, but how this trade-off is managed remains unclear. The Kelch-like ECH-associated protein 1 (KEAP1)–nuclear factor–erythroid 2–related factor 2 (NRF2) pathway, a key regulator of antioxidant defenses, is frequently hyperactivated in cancer. Formaldehyde, a genotoxic one-carbon by-product, is typically detoxified via glutathione (GSH), which is also essential for suppressing ferroptotic cell death. Here, we show that NRF2 promotes formaldehyde tolerance through up-regulation of the cystine transporter SLC7A11, enabling a protective mechanism that is largely independent of GSH, which remains necessary for ferroptosis resistance. In NRF2-active cells, formaldehyde reacts with cysteine to form a thiazolidine conjugate, and the combination of formaldehyde stress and SLC7A11 inhibition activates the integrated stress response, suppresses global protein synthesis, and markedly compromises cell viability. Together, these findings reveal that NRF2 coordinates ferroptosis resistance and formaldehyde tolerance, exposing a cancer vulnerability through combined inhibition of cystine uptake and GSH synthesis.

title: Primary tumor–derived lactate primes prostate cancer cells for a dormant fate
abstract: The metastatic outcome depends on the state of disseminated cancer cells (DCCs) leading to overt metastasis or undergoing dormancy. Before distant organ colonization, primary tumor microenvironment may shape the decision between proliferation and dormancy. Here, we identify lactic acid (LA), a highly abundant environmental metabolite at the primary site in prostate cancer (PCa), as a key inducer of dormant state. LA-uploading PCa cells undergo a proliferation delay, associated with stemness, therapy tolerance, and invasiveness through the nuclear receptor subfamily 2 group F member 1 (COUP-TF1/NR2F1) activation. These traits rely on LA-driven accumulation of lipid droplets (LDs), which serve as reservoirs of lipid-derived acetyl moieties essential for histone acetylation. Notably, the epigenetic reader BRD4 is essential for COUP-TF1 expression and for establishing and maintaining dormancy. In metastatic sites, where LA levels are low, dormant features are lost, allowing DCCs to support metastatic growth. Last, targeting LA-mediated LD formation or BRD4 activation prevents dormancy entry, reducing PCa cell adaptability and increasing vulnerability to antiproliferative therapies.

title: CASTOR1 functional inactivation drives KRAS-mutant NSCLC and therapy resistance by a noncanonical mechanism of tumor suppression
abstract: CASTOR1, a cytosolic arginine sensor and regulator of mTORC1 signaling, is identified here as a tumor suppressor inKRAS-driven non–small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). In aKRASG12Dmouse model,CASTOR1deletion enhances tumor initiation and progression, accompanied by increased proliferation. Although CASTOR1 is rarely mutated or deleted in human cancers, its expression progressively declines during tumor progression and is associated with increased AKT activation and CASTOR1 phosphorylation, consistent with functional inactivation. Loss of CASTOR1 results in constitutive mTORC1 hyperactivation, impaired arginine-dependent regulation of mTORC1 signaling, elevated p-4EBP1 and p-S6 levels, increased AKT and ERK activation, genomic instability, and resistance to KRASG12Dinhibitors. Tumors and tumor-derived organoids deficient in CASTOR1 are resistant to KRAS inhibition, but this resistance can be overcome by cotargeting mTORC1 or dual PI3K/mTOR inhibition. These findings identify CASTOR1 as a critical link between nutrient sensing and oncogenic signaling and reveal its functional inactivation as an important mechanism contributing toKRAS-driven NSCLC progression and therapeutic resistance. The results further support rational combination therapies to overcome KRAS inhibitor resistance in CASTOR1-low NSCLC.

title: Lineage-specific and gestational age–dependent DNA methylation programming orchestrates human placental development
abstract: The human placenta is essential for pregnancy, yet the dynamic regulation of its DNA methylome during development remains poorly understood. To address this, we generated a single base–resolution DNA methylation atlas of human placental trophoblasts across gestation. We identified a lineage-specific methylation program established immediately after implantation, followed by gestational age–dependent methylation accumulation. This program acted as a developmental barrier that coordinated placental maturation and immune homeostasis. By integrating histone modifications and functional perturbations, we revealed a temporal dynamic between H3K27me3 and DNA methylation that silenced proinflammatory loci and a switch from H3K9me3 to DNA methylation at repeat elements to maintain genome stability. Aberrant methylation in preterm placentas underscored the physiological importance of methylation regulation. Using human trophoblast stem cells, we demonstrated thatDNMT1was critically required for maintaining trophoblast methylome integrity and self-renewal, while the DNMT3 family were equally essential for trophoblast survival. Overall, we established a placenta-specific epigenetic framework for human trophoblast development.

title: PhagoID: Quantitative in situ proximity labeling defines the proteomes of bead- and microbe-containing phagosome lumina across species, maturation, and immune activation
abstract: The phagosome is an immune organelle that integrates signals from diverse cargos to drive pathogen killing, tissue homeostasis, and antigen presentation. How this compartment coordinates such diverse functions remains incompletely understood. A comprehensive view of phagosomal composition across cell states and perturbations could accelerate insight into its regulation. Here, we establish PhagoID, a modular proximity labeling approach that enables in situ proteomic profiling of the phagosome lumen in living cells. Applying PhagoID to murine and human macrophages, we define conserved and species-specific phagosomal proteomes that include both canonical lysosomal components and unexpected contributors from nuclear, mitochondrial, and endoplasmic reticulum (ER) compartments. Integrating these proteomes with 25 genome-scale CRISPR screens of phagosomal phenotypes, we identify a network of lumenal proteins that regulate cargo uptake, acidification, antigen presentation, and microbial control highlighting previously unrecognized phagosomal effectors. We next adapt PhagoID to profile the microbe-containing phagosome and compare the sterile bead-containing phagosome to theEscherichia coli–containing phagosome, demonstrating a modestE. colisignature of phagosome remodeling. Comparative analyses further reveal that loss of LAMP1 enhances recruitment of ER-derived proteins to the phagosome, whereas loss of TFEB minimally perturbs the lumenal proteome despite its role in lysosomal biogenesis. Last, cytokine stimulation remodels the phagosome lumen to enrich for proteins involved in antigen presentation and antimicrobial activity in response to type I and II interferons. These data demonstrate that PhagoID delivers a high-confidence, quantitative, and integrative map of the phagosome lumen, revealing previously unidentified axes of organellar communication and regulatory control in innate immunity.

title: SCML2 inhibits PrimPol-mediated DNA replication repriming and regulates replication gap-associated cancer cell vulnerability
abstract: PrimPol-mediated fork repriming generates single-stranded DNA (ssDNA) gaps during DNA damage tolerance (DDT), which, if not properly repaired, can threaten genomic stability. PrimPol is a highly error-prone polymerase. Thus, PrimPol activity should be tightly regulated to fit into DDT and remain low during unstressed DNA replication. Human sex comb on midleg like-2 (SCML2), a Polycomb protein containing MBT repeats, has been identified as a component of the noncanonical PRC1 complex and a regulator of p53 and CHK1 stability. Here, we show that SCML2A is a suppressor of PrimPol. SCML2A directly binds two domains of PrimPol: Its RBR domain binds the C terminus of PrimPol, and its SAM domain binds the amino-terminal AEP domain, thereby inhibiting ssDNA-binding capacity of the AEP domain. SCML2 depletion leads to increased nascent DNA synthesis and accumulation of PrimPol-mediated ssDNA gaps under replication stress. SCML2 depletion also enhances PrimPol engagement during unstressed DNA replication, leading to subsequent accumulation of ssDNA gaps, which are filled by REV1/POLζ-mediated translesion synthesis (TLS) and RAD51-mediated template switching (TS). SCML2 depletion confers cellular hypersensitivity to RAD51 or REV1/POLζ inhibition, which is associated with increased accumulation of ssDNA gaps. Furthermore, CDK2 phosphorylates SCML2A at Ser267, which suppresses RBR-mediated PrimPol interaction. Cyclin E1 overexpression leads to CDK2-mediated SCML2A Ser267hyperphosphorylation, which releases the inhibitory effect of SCML2A on PrimPol and subsequently induces ssDNA gap accumulation. Collectively, we identify SCML2A as a negative regulator of PrimPol.

title: Scalable architecture for measurement-induced squeezed light interferometers
abstract: Scalable interferometers lie at the heart of photonic quantum technologies, but their expansion has been fundamentally limited by optical losses that grow with circuit depth. Here, we introduce and experimentally demonstrate a measurement-induced architecture for multimode squeezed-light interferometers that overcomes this barrier. By shifting complexity from deep optical networks to programmable homodyne measurements, we realize effective transformations within a shallow, low-loss platform. We validate the principle with a six-mode device and extend it to a 400-mode interferometer, marking a leap in scale beyond conventional designs. Crucially, this strategy not only enables scalable squeezed light interferometry but also provides a powerful route to the generation of large-scale entangled states—a key requirement for quantum computing, simulation, and communication. Our results establish measurement-induced circuits as a practical pathway toward noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) applications and future demonstrations of quantum advantage.

title: RAF isoform selectivity of MEK inhibitors and rational design of a covalent ARAF-MEK inhibitor
abstract: Aberrant activation of the RAS/RAF/mitogen-activated protein kinase kinase (MEK)/extracellular signal–regulated kinase pathway is a frequent cause of cancer. Allosteric MEK inhibitors block this pathway by binding RAF-MEK complexes to prevent activation of MEK by RAF. However, how MEK inhibitor potency varies across the three RAF isoforms remains poorly understood. We profiled seven allosteric MEK inhibitors and observed a notable hierarchy of sensitivity: All most potently inhibited CRAF-driven MEK activation while relatively sparing ARAF-driven activation. We identified point mutations in ARAF and CRAF proximate to the MEK inhibitor binding site that markedly altered inhibitor sensitivity. Using a rational design approach, we developed a more potent inhibitor of ARAF-driven MEK signaling, TWG-07-148. Our cryo–electron microscopy structure shows how this acrylamide-containing analog of MEK inhibitor trametinib covalently targets Cys514, a residue unique to ARAF. Our studies highlight the importance of the activating RAF isoform as a determinant of MEK inhibitor sensitivity and provide proof of concept for the development of MEK inhibitors that more effectively block ARAF-driven MEK signaling via covalent targeting of Cys514.

title: Histone methyltransferase NSD2 shapes CD8+ T cell fates through the H3K36me2-Zbtb20 axis
abstract: CD8+T cells, as the most important cytolytic cells in adaptive immunity, can differentiate into distinct subpopulations with specific functions and fates. During this process, CD8+T cells exhibit substantial plasticity in their differentiation trajectory. Notably, epigenetic regulation has emerged as a pivotal mechanism to govern T cell fate decisions. In this study, we demonstrate that the histone methyltransferase NSD2 critically regulates CD8+T cell differentiation during acute viral infection. While NSD2 deficiency enhances the early expansion of activated CD8+T cells, it severely compromises their survival fitness during the contraction phase, leading to a disproportionate collapse of the antigen-specific pool and limiting the establishment of robust long-lived memory. Mechanistically, this defect is driven by the disruption of the H3K36me2-Zbtb20regulatory axis. Furthermore, we show that in the absence of NSD2, CD8+T cells in tumor exhibit an increased proportion but dysfunctional resident memory T cell phenotype. Collectively, our findings highlight a critical role for NSD2 in providing more mechanistic insights into how epigenetic mechanisms fine-tune T cell differentiation.

title: High-throughput droplet-based enzymatic DNA methylome profiling enables single-cell resolution of epigenetic heterogeneity
abstract: DNA methylation is a fundamental epigenetic modification that regulates gene expression, cellular identity, and disease-associated regulatory programs. However, high-throughput single-cell DNA methylation technologies have been limited by DNA degradation, low CpG recovery, and the poor scalability of bisulfite-based methods. Here, we present scEM-seq, a droplet-based single-cell enzymatic methylome sequencing method that integrates barcode ligation within a single emulsification step, followed by postemulsion cytosine-to-uracil conversion. This design substantially reduces DNA loss and enables robust profiling of tens of thousands of single cells per experiment. scEM-seq generates high-quality single-cell methylomes with moderately improved CpG coverage and balanced read utilization compared with other droplet-based microfluidic methods. Applied to peripheral blood mononuclear cells, scEM-seq accurately resolves major immune lineages, and in prostate cancer tissues, it reveals diverse malignant cell states and patient-specific epigenetic and copy number architectures. scEM-seq enables scalable single-cell dissection of epigenetic heterogeneity across diverse biological and disease contexts, broadening the scope of DNA methylation–based studies into cellular regulation and disease.

title: Loss of KAT5-dependent H2A.Z acetylation provokes chromosomal instability in recurrent pregnancy loss
abstract: Placenta defects are one of the major causes of miscarriages, yet the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. We demonstrate that trophoblast-specific depletion of the acetyltransferaseKat5, or introduction of acetylation-defective mutantsKat5-Q377E G380EandKat5-Y47A, induces severe chromosomal instability (CIN) during trophoblast cells division, leading to embryonic lethality. Moreover, mutation of a key lysine acetyltransferase 5 (KAT5) substrate, H2A.Z, via the introduction ofH2az1-K5R K8R K12R K14R(which prevents H2A.Z acetylation), phenocopies the effects of KAT5 loss. Integrated RNA sequencing and CUT&Tag in mouse trophoblast stem cells reveal that KAT5, through H2A.Z acetylation, regulates transcription of key mitotic genes (Aurka,Aurkb, andCenpa). We extend our finding to human trophoblast stem cells, demonstrating a conserved role for KAT5 in preventing CIN. Clinical analysis of placental villi from recurrent pregnancy loss patients with copy number variations revealed reduced expression of KAT5 and acetylated H2A.Z. This study demonstrates that the conserved KAT5–H2A.Z acetylation pathway safeguards chromosomal stability in trophoblast cells, supporting placenta development and successful pregnancy.

title: Direct observations of submesoscale turbulence driving mesoscale eddy leakage
abstract: Understanding oceanic transport and material fate has long relied on observations that primarily resolve mesoscale, largely geostrophic flows, leaving the role of submesoscale turbulence comparatively unobserved and poorly understood. Here, using new high-resolution drifter-cluster experiments with closest initial spacings below 1 km, we provide direct Lagrangian observations of how submesoscale turbulence modifies mesoscale eddy coherence and transport pathways. The clustered drifters resolve intense, transient ageostrophic motions that are fundamentally absent from geostrophic descriptions of eddy behavior. Analyzed in an eddy-centered reference frame, the observations reveal pronounced submesoscale-driven radial dispersion that facilitates substantial water-mass exchange between the eddy core and its periphery in both the mixed layer and the subsurface. Quantitative estimates indicate submesoscale horizontal diffusivity ofO(10 to 100) m2/s and a nonlocal dispersion regime across submesoscales. These results challenge the traditional view of mesoscale eddies as coherent structures containing a persistent water mass, with broad implications for interpreting and predicting the transport and fate of tracers in the ocean.

title: Morphological intelligence for dynamic aerial interactions
abstract: Biological flyers achieve ecological dominance not through flight alone, but by seamlessly integrating aerial locomotion with forceful physical interactions, including snatching prey, perching on irregular surfaces, and operating across diverse media. Translating this agility into aerial robotics demands reconciling a fundamental conflict: impulsive, high-force actions destabilize the flight platform. Here, we present a bio-inspired unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) equipped with a mechanically intelligent impulsive limb that resolves this tradeoff through physical decoupling. An asymmetric bistable impulse module delivers a 2.3-fold extension within 70 ms, while a soft-linkage architecture reduces the transmission of impulsive interaction forces to the airframe. For the tested seven-segment configuration, intrinsic geometric tolerance corresponds to a passive vertical accommodation range of approximately 70% of the fully deployed arm length, reducing the need for precise altitude regulation within the tested range. We demonstrate the system’s multimodal capacity through dynamic in-flight snatching, energy-efficient perching, high-impact solid fracture, and cross-medium capture in viscous fluids, establishing a new paradigm for UAVs executing physically demanding tasks in complex environments.

title: Structural basis for start codon selection by eIF5-mimic proteins
abstract: Start codon selection extensively regulates the cellular proteome and is implicated in cancer and other diseases. The eIF5-mimic proteins (5MPs: 5MP1/BZW2 and 5MP2/BZW2) restrict non-AUG start codon usage and thereby reprogram proteoform expression from mRNAs with alternative start sites, such as the oncogenic c-Myc. Here, using in extracto cryo–electron microscopy (cryo-EM) and biochemical assays, we report how 5MP represses translation dependent on the sequence context at start codons. Cryo-EM structures of 48Spreinitiation complexes (PICs) reveal 5MP1 bound at the A site of the small ribosomal subunit. 5MPs act as initiation factors that stabilize an open PIC conformation, promoting mRNA scanning and inhibiting initiation at suboptimal start codons. We propose to designate 5MP as eIF1S (eukaryotic initiation factor 1 scanning). These findings reveal the structural basis for proteome modulation by 5MPs and may help correct dysregulated translation in disease.

title: Using initial states to identify successful El Niño–Southern Oscillation forecasts 1 year in advance
abstract: El Niño–Southern Oscillation (ENSO) is the primary source of climate predictability on seasonal and longer timescales over much of the globe, but predicting its phase beyond 9 months has remained challenging. Here, we leverage an underappreciated factor in ENSO forecasting: the substantial variation in forecast skill based on the ENSO phase at the time a forecast is issued. Our analysis of transitions between ENSO phases in a dynamical hindcast dataset demonstrates that this variation markedly exceeds intermodel differences in predictive capability. Forecasts initialized during La Niña conditions perform best, with three models correctly predicting transitions to El Niño 1 year in advance over 70% of the time. We present our findings in a simple framework that allows decision-makers to assess the likelihood of a forecast being correct on the basis of the current ENSO state. Applied effectively, these findings could improve long-lead ENSO forecasting strategies, enhancing global risk management.

title: Hemolymph pressure-mediated friction in the tarsus of the desert locust (Schistocerca gregaria)
abstract: The desert locust (Schistocerca gregaria) performs high-acceleration jumps within milliseconds, relying not only on powerful muscles and spring-loaded hindlegs, but also on precise tarsi-substrate interactions. Although the mechanics of jumping have been extensively studied, the mechanisms enabling rapid attachment and detachment remain poorly understood. Here, we characterize the frictional properties of hindleg tarsi under controlled low-speed contact conditions targeting selected loading features associated with jumping. We hypothesize that locusts coordinate tarsal cuticular structures with internal hemolymph pressure to modulate contact mechanics. Using high-speed videography, a suite of advanced microscopic techniques, biomechanical experiments, and biomimetic prototypes, we provide evidence that hemolymph pressure modulates tarsal stiffness and acts together with structural asymmetry to produce direction-dependent frictional responses. This interplay may contribute to adaptive friction tuning associated with jumping. Our findings advance the understanding of locust locomotor biomechanics and suggest design principles for robotic systems requiring rapid and controllable surface engagement.

title: Interferon-λ signaling to maternal dendritic cells protects against congenital Zika virus infection
abstract: Interferon-λ (IFN-λ, type III IFN) mediates antiviral immunity at anatomic barriers, including the maternal-fetal interface. To investigate the effects of IFN-λ during congenital Zika virus (ZIKV) infection, we infected mice lacking the IFN-αβ receptor (Ifnar1−/−) or both the IFN-αβ and IFN-λ receptors (Ifnar1−/−Ifnlr1−/−) at embryonic day 9 and found that loss of maternal IFN-λ signaling resulted in greater transplacental transmission, highlighting a protective effect of IFN-λ at the maternal-fetal interface. To investigate the spatial relationship between ZIKV infection and antiviral responses, we used HiPlex RNAscope on the entire gravid uterus and found that IFN-λ was expressed more proximal to the site of ZIKV infection inIfnar1−/−dams compared toIfnar1−/−Ifnlr1−/−dams. We performed immunophenotyping of the placenta and uterus by flow cytometry and found a decrease in dendritic cells and natural killer (NK) cells in the uterus ofIfnar1−/−Ifnlr1−/−dams compared toIfnar1−/−dams, but NK cell depletion did not affect fetal infection. Using conditional knockout mice, we identified maternal dendritic cells as the key IFN-λ–responsive cell type mediating protection against ZIKV congenital infection. Together, our data support a model in which IFN-λ signaling to maternal dendritic cells increases dendritic cell accumulation in the uterus, which facilitates a protective antiviral response that restricts ZIKV congenital infection.

title: Frequency-dependent fitness effects are ubiquitous in rapidly adapting microbial populations
abstract: In simple microbial populations, the fitness effects of selected mutations are typically assumed to be constant, regardless of mutant frequency. This assumption underpins predictions about evolutionary dynamics, epistasis, and the maintenance of genetic diversity. Here, we systematically test this assumption using beneficial mutations from early generations of theEscherichia colilong-term evolution experiment (LTEE). Using flow cytometry–based competition assays, we find that frequency-dependent fitness effects are the norm rather than the exception, occurring in ∼80% of strain pairs tested. Most competitions exhibit negative frequency dependence, where fitness advantages decline as mutant frequency increases. We demonstrate that the strength of frequency dependence is predictable from invasion fitness measurements, which explain approximately half of the biological variation in frequency-dependent slopes. We also observe violations of fitness transitivity in several strain combinations, indicating that competitive outcomes cannot always be predicted from fitness measured against a single reference strain. High-resolution measurements reveal that frequency dependence changes substantially within the growth cycle, with the net per-cycle effect reflecting the balance of opposing dynamics at different growth phases. Our results demonstrate that, even in a model system designed to minimize ecological complexity, subtle interactions between closely related genotypes create frequency-dependent selection that can fundamentally alter evolutionary trajectories.

title: Electrically reconfigurable dipolar polaritons with highly tunable nonlinearity in a homobilayer microcavity
abstract: Active control over optical nonlinearity in solid-state systems is central to unlocking exotic many-body phenomena and photonic devices. While exciton-polaritons in transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) offer a promising platform, their practical utility is impeded by fixed interactions and a trade-off between nonlinearity and oscillator strength. Here, we report electrically tunable dipolar polaritons in a dual-gated bilayer MoS2microcavity, demonstrating in situ reshaping of the dispersion and modulation of the light-matter coupling strength via the quantum-confined Stark effect. Crucially, this electrical control yields a seven-fold enhancement of the polariton-polariton interaction strength. This enhancement arises from the combined tuning of the effective exciton-exciton interaction and the excitonic Hopfield coefficient. In addition, electrostatic doping provides an independent knob to continuously drive a strong-to-weak coupling crossover. Our findings establish dual-gated TMD homobilayer as a versatile platform for on-chip, dynamically reconfigurable nonlinear light-matter physics.
